summary: ACCEPT at ebe92e39. Item 1 (N3) only - correctly one item per PR. PRODUCER-SIDE is the better choice than the consumer-hardening I specified: one refusal at the source instead of N consumers each needing their own guard, and it cannot be defeated by a consumer nobody enumerated. Verified: normal SELL closure is untouched because _apply_position_fill zeroes the row inside the fill transaction and does not route through this reconciliation override; updated_at is NON-NULLABLE with server_default=func.now() and onupdate=utcnow, so age is genuinely time-since-last-write, and unrelated writes can only make the guard MORE conservative; the bound is derived from the measured 6.648/10.644/19.119s restores plus one 5s poll, with 24.118 holding and 24.119 releasing so a legitimate aged clear stays reachable; and the deferral is logged as [VIRTUAL-CLEAR-DEFERRED] deferred=N of unbacked_positive=M - a denominator on the line from day one. Rollback is a settings flag: 0 restores immediate-clear semantics. Mutation evidence: guard disabled produces 3 focused failures. NOTES, not blocking. (1) When updated_at is None the code treats age as exactly min_age and therefore CLEARS - fail-open on unknown, the same polarity as the boot-hold defect in item 2. It is dead code against a non-nullable column, but the safe direction is DEFER on unknown; worth flipping if the line survives. (2) #824 and #825 now both bound the same phenomenon at 24.119s from opposite sides, so a worst case can stack to ~48s before a legitimate release completes; harmless but it should be stated in the record rather than discovered. (3) Deploy moves OMS - not between 07:00 and 16:00 ET. Actual harm remains UNMEASURED; 3/143 is a positive-evidence lower bound.
